author: Thomas à Kempis
title: Of gratitude for the Grace of God

verses.text: Why seekest thou rest when thou art born to labour?
verses.modernizedText: Why do you seek rest when you are born to labor?

verses.text: Prepare thyself for patience more than for comforts, and for bearing the cross more than for joy.
verses.modernizedText: Prepare yourself for patience more than for comforts, and for bearing the cross more than for joy.

verses.text: For who among the men of this world would not gladly receive consolation and spiritual joy if he might always have it?
verses.modernizedText: For who among the people of this world would not gladly receive consolation and spiritual joy if he could always have it?

verses.text: For spiritual comforts exceed all the delights of the world, and all the pleasures of the flesh.
verses.modernizedText: For spiritual comforts exceed all the delights of the world and all the pleasures of the flesh.

verses.text: For all worldly delights are either empty or unclean, whilst spiritual delights alone are pleasant and honourable, the offspring of virtue, and poured forth by God into pure minds.
verses.modernizedText: For all worldly delights are either empty or unclean, while spiritual delights alone are pleasant and honorable, the offspring of virtue, and poured forth by God into pure minds.

verses.text: But no man can always enjoy these divine comforts at his own will, because the season of temptation ceaseth not for long.
verses.modernizedText: But no one can always enjoy these divine comforts at his own will, because the season of temptation does not cease for long.

verses.text: Great is the difference between a visitation from above and false liberty of spirit and great confidence in self.
verses.modernizedText: There is a great difference between a visitation from above and false liberty of spirit and great confidence in self.

verses.text: God doeth well in giving us the grace of comfort, but man doeth ill in not immediately giving God thanks thereof.
verses.modernizedText: God does well in giving us the grace of comfort, but a person does ill in not immediately giving God thanks for it.

verses.text: And thus the gifts of grace are not able to flow unto us, because we are ungrateful to the Author of them, and return them not wholly to the Fountain whence they flow.
verses.modernizedText: And thus the gifts of grace cannot flow to us, because we are ungrateful to their Author and do not return them wholly to the Fountain from which they flow.

verses.text: For grace ever becometh the portion of him who is grateful and that is taken away from the proud, which is wont to be given to the humble.
verses.modernizedText: For grace always becomes the portion of the grateful person, and what is usually given to the humble is taken away from the proud.

verses.text: I desire no consolation which taketh away from me compunction, I love no contemplation which leadeth to pride.
verses.modernizedText: I desire no consolation that takes compunction away from me; I love no contemplation that leads to pride.

verses.text: For all that is high is not holy, nor is everything that is sweet good; every desire is not pure; nor is everything that is dear to us pleasing unto God.
verses.modernizedText: For all that is high is not holy, nor is everything sweet good; not every desire is pure, nor is everything dear to us pleasing to God.

verses.text: Willingly do I accept that grace whereby I am made humbler and more wary and more ready to renounce myself.
verses.modernizedText: I willingly accept that grace by which I am made humbler, more watchful, and more ready to renounce myself.

verses.text: He who is made learned by the gift of grace and taught wisdom by the stroke of the withdrawal thereof, will not dare to claim any good thing for himself, but will rather confess that he is poor and needy.
verses.modernizedText: The person made learned by the gift of grace and taught wisdom by the blow of its withdrawal will not dare to claim any good thing for himself, but will instead confess that he is poor and needy.

verses.text: Give unto God the thing which is God’s,(1) and ascribe to thyself that which is thine; that is, give thanks unto God for His grace, but for thyself alone confess thy fault, and that thy punishment is deserved for thy fault.
verses.modernizedText: Give to God what is God’s,(1) and ascribe to yourself what is yours; that is, give thanks to God for His grace, but confess your fault as yours alone, and that your punishment is deserved for your fault.

verses.text: Sit thou down always in the lowest room and thou shalt be given the highest place.(2) For the highest cannot be without the lowest.
verses.modernizedText: Always sit down in the lowest place, and you will be given the highest place.(2) For the highest cannot be without the lowest.

verses.text: For the highest saints of God are least in their own sight, and the more glorious they are, so much the lowlier are they in themselves; full of grace and heavenly glory, they are not desirous of vain-glory; resting on God and strong in His might, they cannot be lifted up in any wise.
verses.modernizedText: For the highest saints of God are least in their own sight, and the more glorious they are, the humbler they are in themselves; full of grace and heavenly glory, they do not desire vainglory; resting on God and strong in His might, they cannot be lifted up in any way.

verses.text: And they who ascribe unto God all the good which they have received, “seek not glory one of another, but the glory which cometh from God only,” and they desire that God shall be praised in Himself and in all His Saints above all things, and they are always striving for this very thing.
verses.modernizedText: And those who ascribe to God all the good they have received “do not seek glory from one another, but the glory that comes from God only,” and they desire that God be praised in Himself and in all His Saints above all things, and they are always striving for this very thing.

verses.text: Be thankful, therefore, for the least benefit and thou shalt be worthy to receive greater.
verses.modernizedText: Be thankful, therefore, for the least benefit, and you will be worthy to receive greater.

verses.text: Let the least be unto thee even as the greatest, and let that which is of little account be unto thee as a special gift.
verses.modernizedText: Let the least be to you as the greatest, and let what is of little account be to you as a special gift.

verses.text: If the majesty of the Giver be considered, nothing that is given shall seem small and of no worth, for that is not a small thing which is given by the Most High God.
verses.modernizedText: If the majesty of the Giver is considered, nothing given will seem small and of no worth, for what is given by the Most High God is not a small thing.

verses.text: Yea, though He gave punishment and stripes, we ought to be thankful, because He ever doth for our profit whatever He suffereth to come upon us.
verses.modernizedText: Indeed, even if He gave punishment and stripes, we ought to be thankful, because He always does for our benefit whatever He allows to come upon us.

verses.text: He who seeketh to retain the favour of God, let him be thankful for the favour which is given, and patient in respect of that which is taken away.
verses.modernizedText: Let the person who seeks to retain the favor of God be thankful for the favor given and patient concerning that which is taken away.

verses.text: Let him pray that it may return; let him be wary and humble that he lose it not.
verses.modernizedText: Let him pray that it may return; let him be watchful and humble so that he does not lose it.
